**Project Summary: Nairobi Youth Code Initiative**

The Nairobi Youth Code Initiative will teach practical digital skills to 240 secondary school students at four partner schools, preparing them for higher education, jobs, or starting their own businesses. Kenya's technology sector is growing, but many young people in Nairobi's under-resourced neighborhoods have no access to computers, qualified instructors, or structured learning.

Over two years, the program will deliver a progressive curriculum in web development, Python programming, and problem-solving. Each school will host weekly after-school sessions led by trained facilitators and will have a dedicated computer lab. Students will complete hands-on projects that address community challenges, and top performers will receive mentorship and internship placements with local technology partners. We aim for girls to make up at least 50 percent of enrollment.

The total budget is KES 6.2 million, covering equipment, facilitator training and stipends, curriculum materials, connectivity, mentorship, and evaluation. This works out to roughly KES 25,800 per student. We will measure success through skills assessments, project portfolios, retention rates, and post-program tracking of education and employment outcomes.
